chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muthanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one in Ihram may not get cupping done unless he fears for himself that he will be unable to pray.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: When is a person in Ihram allowed to get cupping done?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of cupping for the Muhrim is not absolute but contingent upon necessity, specifically when the physical toll would impair the performance of Salat, the pillar of worship. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of *darura* (necessity) overriding general prohibitions to preserve the integrity of ritual acts. The ruling underscores the balance between maintaining the sanctity of Ihram and ensuring the Muhrim remains capable of fulfilling his primary religious obligations.
